title: Model catalog demo - Crestwell Health
summary: Redwood AE/SE run a model catalog walkthrough with Crestwell Health. Focus on selecting open models for NER/summarization workloads, reviewing benchmark expectations (latency/cost) and compatibility matrix for Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private. Customer asked about quantization profiles, KV cache impacts, and SOC2/audit artifacts. Agreed next steps: share benchmark spreadsheet, compatibility matrix, and schedule POC scoping call.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we, uh, are Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE and Samir is our SE. Quick intro from you all?
[00:08] Laura Martinez: Hi this is Laura, CTO at Crestwell, we run a mixed infra, some GCP, some on-prem for PHI.
[00:13] Devon Price: Devon, ML eng, working on NER and summarization for clinical notes.
[00:17] Nina Patel: Nina, platform, I'm primarily worried about VPC peering and KMS.
[00:22] Maya Chen: Great, thanks. Today's agenda — quick model catalog demo, show how to pick open models, look at the benchmark table, then walk the compatibility matrix for Hosted / Dedicated / Private and show Console + Optimize suggestions. We'll leave 10 minutes for Q&A.
[00:40] Samir Kapoor: I'll start with the model catalog view in the console. So here's our curated open model list, you can filter by task — for you I'd recommend NER and summarization tuned models like mistral variants or the re-mix family, and also some tuned Llama forks. Note — the transcribe did say "remix" sometimes, sorry the auto text is messy.
[01:05] Laura Martinez: Question: are those families quantized on our side or do you provide quantization profiles?
[01:10] Samir Kapoor: Good Q. We ship a compatibility matrix per model which shows supported quantization profiles (8-bit, 4-bit, int4 simulated), and our Optimize engine recommends quantization profiles based on your token distribution. For example Bluebird-7B (example open model) runs great in 4-bit on A100 w/ our kernel selection, but for high-accuracy NER you might prefer 8-bit HF QAT profiles.
[01:34] Devon Price: Can you clarify "kernel selection" — does Redwood recompile for different hardware?
[01:38] Samir Kapoor: Yes, we select optimized kernels and schedules at deploy time — sometimes the names in the console say "compiled for A100" or "GV100 optimized". Also note our autoscaler respects batch sizes and prefix caching, the KV cache (sometimes transcribed as K-V cash) is preserved across requests in Dedicated and Private.
[02:02] Maya Chen: We'll jump to benchmarks. Here's a benchmark table we run internally — p50/p95 for 512 and 2048 token sequences, throughput and cost-per-token estimates.
[02:12] [screen-share pause / link shared: spreadsheet/crestwell-benchmarks.csv]
[02:20] Samir Kapoor: Important to match your sequence length distro — Devon you mentioned average clinical note ~1k tokens and some long docs up to 3k?
[02:29] Devon Price: Yeah, average 900-1,200 tokens, with 5-10% above 2k.
[02:33] Samir Kapoor: Ok so in our bench for 2048 sequences, mistral-7b-q4 reaches ~45ms p50 on A100 with batching of 4, p95 about 120ms. On GV100 numbers are slightly higher, roughly +30% latency. Costs tracked in the sheet — we estimate per-1000-token cost at $X for hosted baseline, less with Dedicated commit.
[02:55] Laura Martinez: Is that hosted or dedicated numbers?
[02:58] Samir Kapoor: Those are Dedicated A100 numbers; hosted will be similar but variance depends on multi-tenant scheduling. For guaranteed SLOs you'd pick Dedicated or Private.
[03:07] Nina Patel: What about encryption and audit trails? We need SOC2 + HIPAA controls.
[03:12] Maya Chen: We have SOC2 Type II and HIPAA BAAs for enterprise plans; audit logs and KMS/HSM integrations are available for Private and Dedicated. We'll share the security pack.
[03:22] [00:03:30] Speaker 1: (inaudible) sorry, the auto transcript is messing up model names.
[03:28] Samir Kapoor: No worries. Back to compatibility matrix — we show per model whether streaming, function calling, structured output and hardware families are supported. For example some large-opt models don't support KV cache eviction patterns the same way, so the Console will flag them.
[03:48] Devon Price: Are there turnkey evals or regression tests we can plug in?
[03:52] Maya Chen: Yes, Optimize includes eval sets and you can upload your test prompts; we run quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to a prompt set.
[03:58] Devon Price: Nice. Can the Console show recommended model + quantization per route?
[04:02] Samir Kapoor: Exactly — Optimize will suggest a profile per route based on latency/cost SLOs and quality threshold. We'll demo that now.
[04:12] [screen-share: Console -> Optimize -> Route suggestions]
[04:18] Samir Kapoor: Here we took a summarization route, looked at your sample prompts, and the optimizer suggests "mistral-7b-q4 with small batch and prefix caching" or "remix-13b-int8 for higher fidelity but more cost". The UI shows expected p50/p95 and cost delta.
[04:36] Laura Martinez: Does the optimizer consider KV cache hit rate?
[04:40] Samir Kapoor: Yes, it models prefix reuse and KV cache hit ratios, and will prefer models that benefit more from caching for short-turn dialogue. If your workloads have long single-pass docs, it will prioritize per-token efficiency.
[04:52] Nina Patel: For Private deployment, how much ops work is needed? Can we bring our own KMS?
[04:57] Maya Chen: You can bring KMS/HSM, we integrate with major KMS providers. Private includes a control plane we host or hand over (customer-managed), depending on the package. Ops can be minimal if you accept Redwood-managed updates; for air-gapped there's an on-prem bundle.
[05:14] Devon Price: If we do a POC, can we test both Hosted and Dedicated performance and see the compatibility gaps?
[05:19] Samir Kapoor: Yes, POC scoping usually includes a hosted baseline and a dedicated pilot with reserved capacity for a week or two to run benchmarks — we also run your prompt set to validate the optimizer suggestions.
[05:30] Laura Martinez: On pricing, curious about commit tiers for Dedicated and any discounts for model-heavy usage.
[05:35] Maya Chen: We'll send the Dedicated commitment worksheet — typically we offer stepped discounts for sustained usage and enterprise negotiation for private/BAA.
[05:42] [06:00] Speaker 2: small crosstalk, "what about tool-calling"
[05:50] Samir Kapoor: Tool/function calling is supported; the catalog also shows whether a model supports structured tool outputs. In some open models you may need a light post-processing step, which we can do in the runtime.
[06:00] Devon Price: Any gotchas around tokenization differences? We saw different token counts across HF and other runtimes.
[06:06] Samir Kapoor: Yes, tokenizers differ. The compatibility matrix notes tokenization variants; we normalize in the Console and show an "effective token count" used for cost estimates. Sometimes the transcriber shows H-F as "H F" which is odd.
[06:18] Maya Chen: I'll quickly demo the API sample — here's a /generate call, specify model_id, quant_profile, and routing policy.
[06:26] [screen-share: API example pasted: curl -X POST https://api.redwood...]
[06:32] Maya Chen: You can set route=dedicated or route=hosted and we perform smart routing if capacity constrained.
[06:39] Nina Patel: Does smart routing handle regional constraints? We need EU-only data residency for some routes.
[06:44] Samir Kapoor: Yes, routing policies include region and data residency flags. Private obviously keeps data in your VPC/on-prem.
[06:52] Laura Martinez: On quality, do you have real example evals for clinical NER?
[06:56] Samir Kapoor: We have public evals and we can run a Crestwell-specific eval with your prompt sets during the POC.
[07:04] Devon Price: Ok, next steps?
[07:07] Maya Chen: Let's recap. We'll send the benchmark spreadsheet with our Dedicated vs Hosted numbers, a compatibility matrix per model family, and the Dedicated commitment worksheet. Samir will run a targeted latency test for GV100 vs A100 with your 2048 sequence profile. Devon to share prompt set and token distribution.
[07:24] Laura Martinez: Sounds good.
[07:26] Maya Chen: Anything else?
[07:28] Nina Patel: Can you also include the SOC2 / HIPAA docs and a sample BAA?
[07:32] Maya Chen: Yes.
[07:34] [Closing remarks, thanks everyone]
[07:38] Transcript notes: auto-transcription has some errors for model family names and hardware (e.g., GV100 sometimes shows as G-V one), speaker labels occasionally generic.

Devon Price - upload sample prompt set and token-length distribution to the shared drive by 2026-10-09
